report.executive_summary: This handover reconciles the round-1 proposal brief and verification memo for work order WO-01, pump-module selection for a water-reclamation transfer loop. Both documents name P2, and the trusted facts support that choice: all four modules qualify, and P2 draws 12 kWh per common acceptance run, 40 kWh below runner-up P3. The artifacts are nonetheless imperfect. The proposal brief's chart misdraws the bars, mislabels one candidate, leaves a second subfigure blank and truncates its recommendation text. The verification memo recomputes every number correctly but missed the proposal figure's errors and draws its own chart off-scale. Six open questions carry forward; all commercial data remain unverified.
report.figure_caption: Handover illustration: verified per-run energy by candidate with quality and defect labels, beside the round-1 reconciliation chain marking where the proposal chart errors and the verifier's missed figure check arose.

recommendation.rationale: P2 qualifies (quality 97, 1 defect) and minimizes energy at 12 kWh per common acceptance run, 40 kWh below runner-up P3 and 46 below P4's zero-defect build; the lowest-energy rule is decisive and no supplied fact changes the ordering. Round-1 chart defects are presentational and do not alter the ranking.

sections.body: Applying the two policy gates independently to the trusted table: P1 (quality 84, 4 defects), P2 (97, 1), P3 (80, 3) and P4 (81, 0) all qualify — quality at least 80 and at most 5 raw defects. reject_all is inapplicable and no candidate-ID tie-break engages, so energy alone decides: P2 12 kWh, then P3 52, P1 56, P4 58. Gaps to the winner are P3 +40, P1 +44 and P4 +46 kWh; P4 draws about 4.8 times P2's energy. The 40 kWh margin to the nearest challenger far exceeds plausible test variation on the fixed flow and head basis, so both delivered documents correctly select P2.
sections.heading: Reconciled Findings and Decision

sections.body: The proposal brief's prose is accurate, but its illustration is not. Recorded defects: bar heights do not match their values (the 12 kWh bar is drawn far out of scale); the fourth bar is labelled 56/Q84, which are P1's numbers, not P4's; only one bar carries an axis label; the second subfigure is entirely blank; and page-2 text cuts off mid-sentence at the recommendation. The verification memo's arithmetic is correct and its cross-check of A's text reconciles, but it states that A's figure labels contain no slip despite the mislabelled bar, and its own left bar chart is off-scale. sections.heading: Recorded Artifact Quality Issues

sections.body: Measured facts are limited to quality indices, raw defect counts and per-run energy on the shared acceptance basis. Cost, delivery schedules, maintenance profiles and field reliability are unverified for every candidate and may not enter the ranking. Six questions carry forward: (1) is the fixed duty representative of seasonal loop demand; (2) does the acceptance-run basis match commissioning tests for all four modules; (3) obtain field reliability data; (4) request lifecycle cost and spares profiles, notably for P4's zero-defect build; (5) obtain lead-time commitments; (6) verify whether P2's single defect is cosmetic or functional
sections.heading: Measured Facts and Open Questions

sections.body: Recompute eligibility, ranking and gaps directly from the trusted table rather than from any prior figure, since round-1 illustrations were off-scale. Check figure-to-value correspondence explicitly — bar heights, bar labels and axis labels against stated numbers — before endorsing any delivered chart. Ensure recommendation text is complete, not truncated. Keep measured facts separate from unverified commercial items in every claim. Extra emphasis on a non-client candidate, such as repeated zero-defect praise for P4, is legitimate analysis when tied to its stated tracking purpose but must never displace the lowest-energy rule.
